Lesson 1 · Guided route

Build evidence you can trust: guided case

Which lodging offer can we recommend with confidence?

Work through 5 selected steps. The short case gives the decision first; the technical appendix holds the complete model and derivations.

Short caseTechnical appendix
Guided steps
  1. 01. Start with a decision and a data passport
  2. 02. Verify identity before removing duplicates
  3. 03. Calculate a comparable offer, then qualify the choice
  4. 04. A join can multiply the evidence
  5. 05. Leave an audit trail and a bounded recommendation

Guided step 01 / 5

Start with a decision and a data passport

A colleague is comparing two-night stays across the fictional towns of Willow Bay, Cedar Reach and Juniper Vale. The decision is not “find the smallest number.” It is “choose an eligible, comparable offer within a budget.” Evidence must preserve what was observed, for whom, when and under which terms. In this lesson, all quotes and fixtures are newly generated teaching data, not market research.

Write a data passport before calculating: decision, target population, observation unit, fields, collection time, selection rules, provenance and known limits. Our target is the generated set of private-room hotel quotes for two specified arrival dates. We cannot infer availability, service quality or actual prices elsewhere.

  • Decision: shortlist comparable two-night hotel offers.
  • Observation: one lodging × arrival date quote, for one room.
  • Source: local simulation, seed 41021, prices in fictional currency units (CU).
  • Handoff: a comparable table, an audit trail and a bounded recommendation.

Pause and explain

Would “the cheapest hotel in Willow Bay” be supported by this exercise?

Compare your reasoning

No. We observe generated offers for specified dates and terms, not every real hotel or every possible stay. The defensible claim is cheapest among the eligible complete synthetic offers.

Guided step 02 / 5

Verify identity before removing duplicates

The raw lab has 61 rows. One is an exact duplicate introduced to imitate an ingestion retry. Removing that exact repeated record leaves 60 distinct quote rows. The candidate key lodging_id + arrival is then unique. We do not delete all repeated lodging IDs, because the dates are part of the observation.

A duplicate key with different prices is a conflict, not an automatic invitation to keep the first row. Investigate whether the rows refer to different retrieval times, room types or refund terms. If a newer observation supersedes an older one, retain provenance and state the precedence rule. Entity resolution across misspelled names likewise needs recorded evidence and a reversible mapping.

Key check: number of distinct (lodging_id, arrival) pairs = number of rows

Uniqueness is necessary for this table, but not sufficient for truth. A unique row can still have the wrong unit, date or amount.

Pause and explain

Two rows share a key but one costs 80 CU and the other 95 CU. Is drop_duplicates a complete remedy?

Compare your reasoning

No. Exact de-duplication does not resolve conflicting values. Determine whether the observation definition needs another field or whether one value is an error, then document the decision.

Guided step 03 / 5

Calculate a comparable offer, then qualify the choice

The following offers are sorted by the same two-night total, with tax and cleaning handled consistently. Sorting by nightly price alone can reverse a comparison when fixed fees differ. Refundability and walking distance remain separate decision attributes; compressing them into a score requires explicit weights.

Six lowest eligible complete synthetic offers

A ranking is conditional on the chosen outcome and eligibility rules. The cheapest complete observation does not establish best service, best overall value or future availability. A defensible shortlist names the price measure and leaves judgment about other attributes visible.

Pause and explain

If the cheapest offer is nonrefundable, must it be selected?

Compare your reasoning

No. The total answers a cost question. Flexibility is another criterion, and its value depends on the traveler’s needs. Apply an explicit constraint or trade-off instead of pretending price captures everything.

Guided step 04 / 5

A join can multiply the evidence

Each quote needs one walking-distance attribute from a lodging dimension. The safe many-to-one join keeps 37 rows and verifies every key matched. Deliberately duplicating one dimension key creates 39 rows in the unsafe join. A duplicated quote then receives extra weight in later averages.

Join cardinality is part of the analysis
RelationshipExpected key patternTypical safeguard
One-to-oneBoth sides uniqueValidate both keys
Many-to-oneRepeated left keys, unique right keysValidate right key and row-count stability
Many-to-manyBoth sides repeatExplain intended combinations or redesign keys

Record unmatched keys as well as row growth. An inner join can shrink the sample by dropping unmatched observations; a left join preserves them but may introduce missing attributes. Validate cardinality, compare row counts and inspect the match indicator before calculating.

Pause and explain

A join succeeds without an error. Does that prove it is correct?

Compare your reasoning

No. Unless cardinality and coverage were explicitly checked, a syntactically valid join may duplicate or drop observations and change the analysis population.

Guided step 05 / 5

Leave an audit trail and a bounded recommendation

Use a repeatable sequence: detect, decide, correct and document. Checks should cover identity, scope, values and relationships. Every correction should have a reason, a reversible transformation and a measurable consequence such as rows affected. Missingness is an investigation prompt, not an automatic deletion instruction.

A defensible handoff checklist
Audit fieldWhat this lab records
IdentityComposite quote key; fixture + team key
ScopePrivate-room Hotel quotes on two arrival dates
ValuesMissing prices, nonpositive-price flag, explicit tax formula
RelationshipsMany-to-one lodging join; date-aware manager assignment
ReproductionSeed 41021, standalone code, calculated JSON and notebook
LimitSynthetic exercise, no evidence about actual markets or managers

Management handoff: “I compared 37 complete synthetic quotes under a common two-night price definition. I removed one known ingestion duplicate, flagged invalid prices and verified key-safe joins. The shortlist is conditional on eligibility and completeness. Review refundability and trip requirements before selecting an offer.”

Next, Lesson 2 asks what the remaining observations look like. Distributional analysis begins only after the observation, population and preparation choices are defensible.

Pause and explain

What should a colleague be able to do with the handoff?

Compare your reasoning

Rebuild the result from the standalone lab, explain every denominator and exclusion, identify its main limitation, and understand the action the evidence can support.

Compare with the known truth

Reveal the generator truth

The generator deliberately includes one duplicate and three incomplete records in the selected market. Those are known teaching facts, not discoveries about real hotels.
